P1.evidence: No frame of any kind. The prospect took control in the first ninety seconds with 'I'm going to make it short for you. How much is it?' and never gave it back. Prior contact was referenced but nothing was read back - 'I think you've been in contact with us like three months ago, right?' The only version of the open question came six minutes in, as a leading multiple choice: 'do you feel like you want to have the customization specifically to you, have like programs that change over time, have someone to ask your questions, did you actually learn everything yourself, or what is it that you're mainly looking for?'

P2.evidence: Not a single baseline question was asked. Age, height, weight, health conditions, injuries, diet, sleep and energy are all completely unknown after the call. Occupation and training history came out only because the prospect volunteered them while explaining why he was rushing. The one fact that most needed following up - 'it's been two and a half years since I've done anything' after a lifetime of training - drew only the rep repeating it back.

P3.evidence: No goals work at all. Nothing was asked about what he wants to look like, what he cannot currently do, what is driving this, or who else it affects.

P4.evidence: Never run. The prospect handed over the entire root cause unprompted - a lifetime of training that stopped dead at COVID and never restarted, plus a working life so fragmented he took five other calls during this one - and none of it was picked up.

P5.evidence: Never run. There was a clear opening in 'this is driving me crazy' after two and a half years and it was not taken.

P6.evidence: Never run. No commitment check of any kind preceded the price being named.

P11.evidence: Applicable, because the prospect volunteered to buy: 'I'll fill whatever up, give you my credit card, and we can start on Monday.' Nothing was done with it. No payment taken and no link sent, no Trevor onboarding booked, no agreement, no community access. The step actually taken was to promise an email of options for the prospect to work through alone.

objection_plays.detail: The prospect opened on money and stayed there: 'How much is it? Because it's all about the money.' None of the play ran. No isolate, no reframe from SHOULD-I to HOW, no permission question, no financial picture. The rep briefly tried to defer the number - correctly - and then supplied a $1,000 to $7,000 range a minute later, before any value existed and before he knew a single fact about the man.

A textbook not-the-right-time trigger, delivered at length: 'my time here is crazy, believe me. It's like, I had no time. I'm only here for a month and a half... I have three houses that I'm working on right now, and it's crazy. My time here is like, I had to clone myself.' Nothing ran - not 'things never slow down', not 'when does it actually become the right time', not 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled', which is precisely the answer to a man juggling three building sites.

No clinical screening step exists and nothing was asked. A man who trained his whole life and has done nothing for two and a half years was moved toward a purchase with no question about age, weight, injuries, conditions or medication.

notes: A referred, high-intent prospect who offered his credit card unprompted, and the process ran at almost zero. The single coachable point is the one that repeats across this batch: he answered a price question with an invented range inside two minutes rather than converting the prospect's own urgency into a booked, structured conversation. Given the time pressure the right move was to take the credit card there and then or book a firm fifteen minutes, not to promise an email.
